properties.natural_language: All JSON messages received on the Stratum TCP connection must be valid JSON terminated with a linefeed (LF) character before any further processing occurs.
Hex values in Stratum protocol messages must be lowercase, must not have a 0x prefix, and must use the minimum number of significant digits.
For mining.submit messages, the worker token must be a valid token issued during the current session's mining.authorize exchange before the submission is accepted.
For mining.submit messages, the job ID must match an active job currently assigned to the session; stale or unknown job IDs must be rejected.
Mining configuration received via mining.set must have an extranonce of at most 6 bytes, and epoch and target values must be valid before the miner uses them for hashing.
Mining jobs received via mining.notify must contain a valid job ID, block number, and header hash in correct hex format before the miner begins hashing.
After a successful mining.hello exchange, both client and server have agreed on protocol version, compression support, and session timeout parameters.
After a successful mining.subscribe, the session ID returned by the server must be unique and unpredictable, and the session is recorded in the server's session cache.
After mining.authorize succeeds, each authorized worker receives a unique token that is bound to the current session and cannot be used across sessions.
The session error counter must monotonically increase for each error detected and the server must disconnect the client when the counter reaches or exceeds the maxerrors threshold.
A session must transition through states strictly in order: TCP-connected → hello → subscribed → authorized → mining-active. No state may be skipped.
After a successful session resumption, the server must return the same session ID and restore the previously assigned extranonce and active jobs without requiring re-authorization.
When a session ID is not found in the cache during resumption, the server must create a new session with a new ID, and the client must re-authorize all workers.

Error codes must be correctly classified: 2xx for conditional errors, 3xx for authentication errors, 4xx for syntax errors, and 5xx for server errors. Each classification must be deterministic for the same error condition.
The idle timeout mechanism must disconnect clients that send no messages (including mining.noop keepalives) within the negotiated timeout period.
Before executing SLOAD, the transaction must have at least 800 gas remaining (EIP-1884 repriced cost). Contracts assuming the old 200 gas cost may revert unexpectedly.
Before executing BALANCE or EXTCODEHASH, the transaction must have at least 700 gas remaining per the EIP-1884 repriced schedule.

The gas schedule must be applied consistently: after EIP-1884 activation, SLOAD always costs 800 gas, BALANCE always costs 700 gas, and EXTCODEHASH always costs 700 gas, regardless of calling context.
After SELFBALANCE (0x47) executes successfully, the EVM stack contains the current contract's balance at the top, and exactly 5 gas has been consumed.
SELFBALANCE must return the same value as BALANCE(ADDRESS) for the currently executing contract, but at lower gas cost (5 vs 700+ gas).
Contracts using SLOAD within a 2300 gas stipend (transfer/send fallback) will always revert after EIP-1884 activation, since 800 > 2300 - LOG overhead.
After gas deduction, if remaining gas is negative, execution must immediately revert with an out-of-gas exception; no trie access may occur.
The gas validation check must always occur before the actual trie access operation, never after, to prevent state reads on insufficient gas.
The block timestamp used in the difficulty calculation must be validated as greater than the parent block's timestamp before computing the adjustment factor.
Uncle references in the parent block must be cryptographically verifiable via the unclesHash field in the block header before using the uncle count in difficulty calculation.
After computing the adjustment factor, the result must be bounded between -99 and uncle_factor (1 or 2), inclusive. The formula is max(uncle_factor - ((timestamp - parent.timestamp) // 9), -99).
After difficulty computation, the child difficulty must equal parent.difficulty + (parent.difficulty // 2048) * adjustment_factor. The difficulty must never be zero.
The uncle factor must be exactly 1 when the parent block has no uncles, and exactly 2 when the parent block has one or more uncles. No other values are valid.

The EIP-100 difficulty formula must produce identical results across all client implementations for the same inputs (parent difficulty, parent timestamp, block timestamp, uncle presence) to maintain consensus.

Including uncle presence in the difficulty calculation must normalize the total block production rate (canonical + uncle blocks) to maintain a constant average target time, preventing issuance gaming.
All stack-only environment opcodes (ADDRESS, ORIGIN, CALLER, CALLVALUE, CALLDATASIZE, CODESIZE, GASPRICE, RETURNDATASIZE) must charge exactly GAS_BASE (2 gas) and push exactly one value to the stack.
Before accessing an external account's data (BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, EXTCODEHASH), the address must be checked against the warm access list to determine the correct gas cost.

After a cold account access, the target address must be added to the warm access list so that subsequent accesses in the same transaction are charged GAS_WARM_ACCESS (100 gas) instead of GAS_COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS (2600 gas).
For RETURNDATACOPY, the offset + size must not exceed the current return data buffer size. Violation must cause an immediate execution revert.

Copy operations (CALLDATACOPY, CODECOPY, RETURNDATACOPY) must charge gas as GAS_VERY_LOW + GAS_COPY * ceil(size/32) + memory_expansion_gas. The total gas must be deducted before any memory write occurs.
After BLOBHASH executes with an index that is within bounds of blob_versioned_hashes, the correct versioned hash is on the stack. If out of bounds, zero is pushed.
After BLOBBASEFEE executes, the current blob base fee from the block environment is pushed to the stack, and GAS_BASE gas is consumed.
SELFBALANCE must always charge exactly GAS_FAST_STEP (5 gas), regardless of whether the executing contract's address is in the warm access list. It must never trigger cold access pricing.
EXTCODEHASH must return zero for empty accounts (balance=0, nonce=0, code=empty) and for non-existent accounts. For accounts with code, it must return keccak256(code).

Before a transaction is accepted for inclusion, the sender's CodeHash must be retrieved from state and verified to equal EMPTYCODEHASH (0xc5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470).
The EIP-3607 CodeHash check must occur after nonce verification to ensure the sender account exists in state before querying its code hash.
If the sender's CodeHash does not equal EMPTYCODEHASH, the transaction must be rejected and must not be included in any block.
If the sender's CodeHash equals EMPTYCODEHASH, the transaction passes the EIP-3607 check and may proceed to further validation steps.

Blocks received from network peers must have every transaction validated against EIP-3607: all transaction senders must have CodeHash == EMPTYCODEHASH. A single invalid transaction invalidates the entire block.
After the address collision attack sequence, even if an attacker finds a collision address and deploys code, any subsequent transaction from that address must be rejected by EIP-3607.
The EIP-3607 check must be applied consistently across all client implementations at the same point in transaction validation to prevent consensus failures.
For eth_call and eth_estimateGas RPC simulation requests, the EIP-3607 sender code check may be skipped to allow simulation of transactions from contract addresses.
For real transaction submissions (eth_sendRawTransaction), the EIP-3607 code check must never be bypassed regardless of the caller's context.

Inclusion list messages received on the gossipsub topic must have transaction data size within MAX_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST (8192 bytes). Messages exceeding this limit must be REJECTED with peer score penalty.
The slot in an inclusion list message must equal the current slot or the previous slot. Messages with any other slot value must be REJECTED.
The validator_index in an inclusion list must be verified as a member of the inclusion list committee for the specified slot. Non-members must be REJECTED with peer score penalty.
The BLS signature on each SignedInclusionList message must be cryptographically valid for the signing validator's public key. Invalid signatures must be REJECTED with peer score penalty.
Each validator may submit at most 2 valid inclusion lists per slot. The third and subsequent submissions from the same validator in the same slot must be IGNORED (dropped without peer penalty).

REJECT-level validation failures must always penalize the sending peer's score. IGNORE-level failures must never penalize the peer's score. This distinction must be maintained throughout the entire validation pipeline.
After all validation checks pass, the inclusion list message must be both accepted locally for processing and forwarded to gossip peers.
Inclusion list timing constraints must be checked: messages must arrive before the attestation due time for the specified slot. Late messages are IGNORED.
The inclusion_list_committee_root in the message must match the actual committee root computed for message.slot on the current chain branch. Mismatches are IGNORED.
Responses to inclusion_list_by_committee_indices requests must contain at most MAX_REQUEST_INCLUSION_LIST (16) SignedInclusionList items matching the requested slot and committee indices.

The validation pipeline for inclusion list messages must apply checks in strict order: tx size → slot → timing → committee root → committee membership → submission limit → BLS signature. No check may be reordered.
All block context read opcodes (COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT, CHAINID) must charge exactly GAS_BASE (2 gas) and push exactly one 256-bit value to the stack.
BLOCKHASH requires at least 1 element on the stack (the requested block number) and at least 20 gas remaining. Stack underflow or insufficient gas must halt execution.

BLOCKHASH must return zero for: future blocks (number > current), the current block (number == current), and blocks older than 256 blocks (number < current - 256). Only blocks in range [current-256, current-1] return the actual hash.
BLOCKHASH must charge exactly GAS_BLOCK_HASH (20 gas), while all other block context opcodes charge exactly GAS_BASE (2 gas). These costs are fixed and must not vary by execution context.
Block instructions that push a value to the stack must check for stack overflow (stack depth == 1024) before pushing. BLOCKHASH must additionally check for stack underflow (needs 1 input).
PREVRANDAO must return the randao_mix from the parent beacon block, which validators can influence only through their own randao reveal but cannot fully predict or control.
CHAINID must return an immutable value that identifies the network. This value must not change during execution or across blocks on the same network.
TIMESTAMP must return a monotonically increasing value that approximates real-world Unix time. The value is set by the block producer and verified by consensus rules.
All bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR) must charge exactly GAS_VERY_LOW (3 gas). This cost is fixed regardless of operand values.

After AND/OR/XOR executes, the result on the stack must be exactly the bitwise operation applied to the two 256-bit input operands. After NOT, the result must be the bitwise complement of the single input operand.
BYTE(i, x) must return the byte at big-endian position i (0=most significant) from the 256-bit word x. For i >= 32, it must return 0.
SHL with shift < 256 must return (value << shift) masked to 2^256-1. SHR must return value >> shift (zero-filled). SAR must return arithmetic right shift (sign-extended).
For shift >= 256: SHL and SHR must return 0. SAR must return 0 if the input is non-negative, or MAX_VALUE (2^256-1) if the input is negative (sign bit set).
All bitwise operations must be constant-time for same-size inputs to prevent timing side-channel attacks that could leak operand values.
Binary bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR) must pop exactly 2 operands and push 1 result. NOT must pop exactly 1 operand and push 1 result. Net stack effect is -1 for binary, 0 for NOT.
The EVM stack depth must never exceed 1024 elements. PUSH and DUP operations that would cause the stack to exceed this limit must raise a StackOverflowError.
After PUSH_N executes, the stack has one additional element (the N-byte big-endian value read from bytecode), and the program counter has advanced by 1+N positions.
After POP executes, the stack has exactly one fewer element (the topmost element is discarded), GAS_BASE is consumed, and PC advances by 1.
DUP_N requires the stack to have at least N elements (item_number < len(stack)). If the stack is too shallow, execution must halt with StackUnderflowError.
After DUP_N executes successfully, the element at position N from the top is copied to the top of the stack. The stack grows by one element and the original element remains in place.
SWAP_N requires the stack to have at least N+1 elements (item_number < len(stack)). If the stack is too shallow, execution must halt with StackUnderflowError.
After SWAP_N executes successfully, the top stack element and the element at position N are exchanged. Stack depth remains unchanged.
Stack bounds checking must always occur before any stack access operation. The check (item_number < len(stack)) must be performed for every DUP and SWAP instruction without exception.

PUSH0 charges GAS_BASE (2 gas), PUSH1-PUSH32 charge GAS_VERY_LOW (3 gas), POP charges GAS_BASE (2 gas), and DUP/SWAP charge GAS_VERY_LOW (3 gas). These costs must be consistent across all implementations.
The program counter must only be modified through explicit PC increment operations (by 1 for simple opcodes, by 1+N for PUSH_N). No other mechanism may alter the PC during stack operations.
Bytecode is immutable during execution. PUSH operations read immediate bytes from bytecode at fixed offsets and these bytes cannot be altered by any instruction during the same execution context.
